title: Introduce SSE span checkpointing with sticky-tail suppression for stable JSON emission
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: Intermittent partial-JSON emissions in our OpenAI-compatible SSE adapter were correlated with long tail fragments and late-arriving delimiters which caused downstream clients to receive non-atomic JSON objects. This PR adds a lightweight span-checkpointing mechanism inside the SSE parser and a sticky-tail suppression heuristic that defers emission of ambiguous trailing fragments for a short, configurable window. The intent is to reduce spurious partial JSON events while preserving low-latency streaming for well-formed events. Summary of changes: 1) Parser: introduce span checkpoints that record byte offsets and event boundaries; checkpoints are emitted as metadata events to the internal stream ledger to enable deterministic reassembly on reconnect or replay. 2) Sticky-tail suppression: when the parser sees a fragment that ends with a likely-truncated JSON token (heuristic based on trailing commas, open braces, unfinished string escapes, or cut-off numeric tokens) it holds emission for up to 120ms (configurable) awaiting completion; if completion does not arrive it emits a guarded partial object with a diagnostic field for downstream operators. 3) Compatibility shim: OpenAI-compat adapter now annotates checkpoint metadata using the existing sse-meta header (no protocol change for most clients); adapter will gracefully ignore checkpoints it's not able to apply. 4) Observability: add metrics for held_fragments_count, checkpoint_emitted, sticky_tail_timeouts and tracing spans for checkpoint lifecycle. 5) Tests: add unit and integration tests that simulate staggered fragment arrival, reconnect with ledger replay, and client-side reassembly. Backwards-compatibility note: default behavior keeps latency-sensitive streams unchanged for well-formed events; only streams with ambiguous tails get the short hold window and diagnostic partials if timed out. Rollout plan: feature gated by env SSE_SPAN_CHECKPOINT=true; staged rollout to canary, then 10% traffic for 48h with metrics alerting on sticky_tail_timeouts > 0.02% of events. Checklist: [x] Parser implementation and benchmarks; [x] Adapter compatibility shim; [x] Unit tests; [x] Integration tests with ledger replay; [x] Observability and dashboards; [x] Feature flag and rollout plan. Related: ENG-7321 (streaming stability), ENG-7550 (client-facing partial JSON incidents). See docs: docs/compatibility/sse-span-checkpointing.md for operator guidance and SDK changes required for advanced reassembly.

b9d4c2e: implement sticky-tail heuristic and emission hold window

review_comments: Marco Li: Important improvement. Two requests before approving: please reduce default hold window to 120ms from 200ms and add a small microbenchmark comparing latency P50/P95 with feature off vs on; also add an explicit opt-out env for high-frequency streams.
Aisha Patel (author): Reduced default to 120ms, added microbenchmark in tests/benchmarks/sse_hold_bench.go and implemented SSE_SPAN_SUPPRESS_DISABLE env flag to opt-out of holding; pushed fixes.

Ellen Rivera: Looks good, one nit on naming: suggest checkpoint->span_checkpoint to avoid collision with existing checkpoint metrics; please add migration note to docs for operators that parse sse-meta.
Aisha Patel (author): Renamed metric and added migration snippet and example in docs/compatibility/sse-span-checkpointing.md; updated dashboards.
Samir Doshi: Verified integration test behavior locally against the adapter; CI rerun passed. Approving.
ci_checks: unit-tests: first run had an intermittent failure on sse_parser_test.go line 127, flake; rerun passed
benchmarks: added bench result artifacts, baseline attached
release_notes: Fixes intermittent partial JSON emissions in SSE streams by introducing span checkpointing and a sticky-tail suppression hold window. Default behavior preserves latency for well-formed events; feature is gated by SSE_SPAN_CHECKPOINT flag. Adds metrics and diagnostics for held fragments and checkpoint lifecycle.
compatibility_impact: Minimal for most clients. Clients that manually parse sse-meta and expect exact event payload ordering should review docs/compatibility/sse-span-checkpointing.md. Adapter only adds metadata and is backwards compatible.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover heuristics for truncated tokens and guard-output behavior. Integration tests simulate staggered arrival, reconnect+ledger replay, and assert that reassembly yields original JSONs or guarded partials on timeout. Canary rollout observed sticky_tail_timeouts under 0.01% with no uptick in client errors.
notes: Operability: dashboards updated (Observability->SSE->SpanCheckpoints) and alerts created: alert if sticky_tail_timeouts rate exceeds 0.05% over 1h. SDKs do not require changes for default behavior; advanced reassembly consumers can opt-in to ledger replay semantics.
